================================================================================
                    SMART EXPENSE TRACKER REST API - FEATURES
================================================================================

1. ADD AN EXPENSE (POST /expenses)
   - Generates a unique UUID v4 identifier for every expense record.
   - Accepts payload fields:
     * id: UUID v4 (auto-generated)
     * title: String (required, non-empty)
     * amount: Number (required, strictly greater than 0)
     * category: String (required, non-empty)
     * date: String (required, valid ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD format)
   - Returns HTTP status 201 Created on success.
   - Automatically trims whitespace on string fields.

2. VIEW ALL EXPENSES (GET /expenses)
   - Returns an array of all expense records stored in expenses.json.
   - Returns HTTP status 200 OK.

3. FILTER EXPENSES BY CATEGORY (GET /expenses?category=Food)
   - Filters the returned expense records by category name.
   - Matches categories case-insensitively (e.g., "?category=food" matches "Food").
   - Returns an empty array if no expenses match the specified category.

4. CALCULATE TOTAL EXPENSES (GET /expenses/summary)
   - Computes financial summary across all recorded expenses:
     * totalExpenses: Overall sum of all expense amounts.
     * categoryTotals: Object containing total sum grouped by each category (e.g., {"Food": 800, "Travel": 700}).
   - Automatically rounds totals to 2 decimal places to prevent floating-point precision artifacts.
   - Returns HTTP status 200 OK.

5. DELETE AN EXPENSE (DELETE /expenses/:id)
   - Deletes an expense record matching the provided UUID parameter.
   - Returns HTTP status 200 OK with confirmation message and deleted record details.
   - Returns HTTP status 404 Not Found with descriptive error JSON if the ID does not exist.

6. ATOMIC JSON FILE STORAGE (utils/fileStorage.js)
   - Stores all expense data inside a local JSON file (expenses.json).
   - Implements atomic writes using temporary staging files (.tmp) and fs.renameSync to prevent data corruption.
   - Uses an in-memory asynchronous promise mutex queue to serialize concurrent write operations safely.
   - Gracefully handles empty or missing JSON files by auto-initializing an empty array structure.

7. REQUEST BODY VALIDATION MIDDLEWARE (middleware/validateExpense.js)
   - Pre-validates incoming POST /expenses requests before they reach the controller.
   - Validates that title, amount, category, and date are present and of correct types.
   - Enforces positive numerical amounts (> 0) and strict ISO YYYY-MM-DD date formatting.
   - Returns HTTP 400 Bad Request immediately with an array of descriptive error details if validation fails.

8. CENTRALIZED ERROR HANDLING MIDDLEWARE (middleware/errorHandler.js)
   - Standardizes JSON error response formatting across all endpoints.
   - Captures malformed JSON syntax errors from request bodies.
   - Maps operational errors to appropriate HTTP status codes (400, 404, 500).

9. CLEAN LAYERED ARCHITECTURE
   - Routes (src/routes/expenseRoutes.js): Define RESTful HTTP verbs and paths.
   - Controllers (src/controllers/expenseController.js): Orchestrate HTTP request/response flow.
   - Services (src/services/expenseService.js): Encapsulate domain logic and mathematical aggregations.
   - Middleware (src/middleware/): Isolate validation and cross-cutting error handling.
   - Storage Utilities (src/utils/fileStorage.js): Manage atomic disk persistence.

10. COMPREHENSIVE AUTOMATED TESTING (tests/expense.test.js)
    - Full Jest + Supertest integration testing suite.
    - Uses an isolated temporary test database (expenses.test.json) to avoid modifying development data.
    - Tests positive CRUD workflows, validation failures, category filtering, summary calculations, and 404 errors.
